+- A live formula scores only if the grader's LibreOffice recalculation resolves it to a value;
+  when recalculation fails, the cell is written out as an error string (#N/A / #NAME? /
+  #VALUE!) and scores 0. Recalculation is unreliable for dynamic-array functions (UNIQUE, SORT,
+  FILTER, SEQUENCE), for a formula that references cells already holding such spilled results,
+  and for deeply nested modern-function formulas (e.g. TEXTJOIN or TEXT wrapping WORKDAY / other
+  date functions). When the expected answer is a plain number, date, or text and your formula
+  would fall into one of these cases, compute the result in Python and write the LITERAL value
+  instead of the formula.
+- When a task SPLITS or EXTRACTS substrings from a text value (e.g. separating a sentence into
+  parts on delimiter words, or pulling fields out of a code string), treat every extracted piece
+  as text and write it as a string — do not parse a date- or number-looking fragment into a
+  datetime or number, even if a worked-example cell in the range appears stored as a date or
+  number, unless the instruction explicitly asks for that piece to be a number or date.
